label: copy phase: letter p is being output now or within the next 2 steps
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (it essentially never fires in the original or delimiter phases) and anticipates the letter p in the output stream. 68% of steps that output p are active (16.6x lift) and they carry 42% of the activation mass. Steps where p is the next output are also active (53%, 12.9x), and so to a lesser degree are steps two outputs before a p. Activation is largest when p is output right after <DEL> (recall_idx 1): every top example (about 0.85-1.0 of max) is an original sequence starting X p p ..., and activation decays over later p outputs in a run. There is a weaker, diffuse tail on other outputs, mostly o, r, f, a (lift 3-5x), plus small activations elsewhere in the copy phase, which explains the incomplete precision and recall. The predicate covers 82% of mass on dev. Not driven by the input token identity, L, digits, or first token.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: p, o, r, f, a, 3; least: y, w, v, e) and the next token to output (most: p, r, o, f, 2, k; least: w, c, e, v); timing cues that raise it most: phase=2, recall_idx=1, L=8 & t=4.
